Every country boy's dream. Basically, it's the equivalent of a Bug.
The basic cabin for Redneck. They say you can spit holes in it.
Artisanal modification of the basic cabin, most likely made by a fellow mechanic for a cup of something strong.
Late model Redneck cabin, generally holding up well.
Redneck native bodywork. Be sure to lock the back door or they'll steal what's inside.
Redneck native bodywork. Be sure to lock the back door or they'll steal what's inside.
A campervan for camping somewhere in the remote wilderness. Often used by explorers.
The best body for a Redneck. It's not very spacious, alas, but that's more than compensated for by its armour plating
Farm tracktor, hauler, bulldozer? You want it? It's yours my friend, as long as you have enough money!
A farm cabin. Inside there is a strong smell of earth, diesel, and fried potatoes. They say that the name comes from an ancient story, but nobody knows which one.
Ideal for demolition work on the few old world buildings still standing.

A farming town that can afford such a tractor variation automatically becomes the local centre. And not for nothing - this machine is a real mobile fortress, and the engine power is enough for any burden.
The car of a true daredevil. Speed, coupled with the ability to put two guns on one of the modifications, makes the Tornado a very attractive purchase for vagrants.
Civic cabin with no weapons, designed solely for racing.
Lightweight and with a powerful engine, but poor armament. For those who like to make a quick buck.
By sacrificing appearance and a bit of speed, the result is something between a prestige car and a bucket. But at least you can rob caravans without the risk of getting a bullet in the petrol tank.
Have you ever tried to make a machine gun out of a tin can? This is it, but the cabin.

Have you ever tried to make a machine gun out of a tin can? This is it, but the cabin.
Simple bodywork, minimal luggage space. Not suitable for trading at all.
A modification of the standard body. Has more armour and additional slots on the sides.
Perhaps the only vulnerability for the modified Tornado. For peaceful times, it is indeed an armoured body. In real combat, this will not be enough.

Those who are successful but live in the bourgeois west choose the Chief Bert for its excellent balance of payload and armament. Faster than its eastern counterpart, however, it is more expensive to maintain.
It's an old army cabin. No amenities and, strangely, no proper weaponry. Ambitious driver will replace it at the earliest opportunity.
A later model of the Chief Bert cab. Superior to the Private in all characteristics.
Heavily-modified cabin of the latest generation. Perfectly armed and protected.
A very unorthodox cabin. It has a peaceful, harmless appearance... And nests for heavy weapons. Most often used by explorers because of these features.
The poorly protected body is covered with a blistered tarpaulin.
Very spacious and well protected body. Most often used by entrepreneurs for transporting workers.
Despite its impressive size, this body does not boast a large cargo capacity: the lion's share of the space is taken up by the equipment for weapons and the pump of a certain 'Iovich'.
Despite its civilian appearance, it has the best armour. Unfortunately, it does not boast either powerful armament or capacity.
The cab of the Cumbine. No more, no less.
The foundation of the basics of any farming operation, because even in a post-disaster world, no one wants to harvest by hand.
